source.publisher: FHWA, 2024 Edition Standard Highway Signs (phased releases 1-6; final release 2026-02-10)
source.rights: MUTCD 11th Ed. Rev. 1, Section 1D.06 P1: traffic control device designs in the Manual are public domain except the Interstate Shield, 511 Travel Information pictograph, National Scenic Byway graphic, and items under FHWA stewardship or ownership. Such items are flagged 'restricted' and kept in restricted/.
source.selection: Per code/variant: newest release; smallest fabrication size (all sizes listed in sizeInches). Sanitized: Illustrator private data, comments and ids removed; class styles inlined. Path data is unchanged.

gaps.textReferences: MUTCD 11th Ed. Rev. 1 text also names R3-8xa/xb/xc (figure labels), R10-4b (legacy range in 2A text), W4-9 series (Part 6 bikeway detour text), W8-15P (6H.34; SHS lists W8-15aP), and W19-7aP (2C.63 heading; SHS lists W16-7aP). None is a separate design in the 2024 SHS status list, and no FHWA vector file exists for them.
gaps.legacy2004: Every sign code extracted from the MUTCD 11th Ed. Rev. 1 text (1,072 distinct) is either in the 2024 SHS status list, discontinued, or one of the textReferences above. So no 2004 SHS or 2012 Supplement carryover design was identified. Those books are PDF-only (https://mutcd.fhwa.dot.gov/SHSe/shs_2004_2012_sup.pdf). Codes that appear only inside raster figure art would not be caught by text extraction.

variants.conversion: Derived sign face, not an FHWA-published SVG. FHWA publishes R6-3a only as dimensioned layout PDFs. The face was extracted from the official 30x24 PDF content stream: the fill and stroke paths painted in the face inks (Separation White, CMYK 0/0/0/1 black) were kept with their PDF coordinates (y axis flipped, rounded to 0.001 pt). All text objects (dimension labels) and every path in the annotation inks (PANTONE 1805 red, CMYK cyan) were dropped, along with the page-sized clip paths. CMYK black maps to #231f20 and White to #fff, matching FHWA's own SVG export of the sibling R6-3.

derived.procedure: Content stream parsed operator by operator; kept 21 face paths (white background, 0.5 pt outline, black border, white panel, 14 letters, 2 arrowheads, 1 shaft body); dropped 12 text objects, 96 annotation paths and 11 page-sized clips.
derived.verification: At 1200 px, rsvg-convert of this file matches poppler/cairo renders of the source PDF everywhere outside a 4 px dilation of the red/cyan annotation inks, except anti-aliasing on the 0.5 pt outline hairline at the page edge (228 px >30% difference on cairo, all on the rounded outer edge). The border, DIVIDED and side bands are also identical to FHWA's R6-3 SVG. The same procedure on the 36x30 PDF gives an equivalent face (20 paths, without the hairline outline).
derived.limits: Not byte-identical to any FHWA SVG; none exists. Face pixels hidden under annotation ink could not be compared directly, but no face path is altered and annotations are separate objects. Coordinates rounded to 0.001 pt.
